questions: What is the 'absolute degree value'? Is it the absolute value of the angle in degrees (i.e., abs(math.degrees(x))), or is it the absolute value of the element after converting to degrees (i.e., math.degrees(abs(x)))?
For sorting, if two elements have the same absolute degree value, is there a secondary sort key? If so, what is it (e.g., original value, index, something else)?
Should the line chart be plotted with plt.plot(cumsum) directly, or should we create a figure and axes explicitly (e.g., fig, ax = plt.subplots())?
Is the cumulative sum computed on the sorted list as a numpy array of floats or integers? Should the return type match the input type (e.g., ints remain ints)?
Does 'ascending order' mean smallest absolute degree value first (i.e., increasing), or largest first (i.e., decreasing)?
Should the function create a new matplotlib figure each call, or reuse/refer to the current figure? Is plt.clf() or plt.close() needed?
What should happen if the input list contains non-numeric elements (e.g., strings)?
Is the x-axis 'Index' meant to be the position in the sorted list (0,1,2,...) or the original indices?
